Verified 12 Nov 2026 on c4, engine 5.8.4, no Visual Studio installed.

- **Enabling Unreal MCP for every target turns a Blueprint-only project into a code project.**
  UAT prints "has no code, but is being treated as a code-based project ... because:
  ModelContextProtocol plugin is enabled", and then needs a compiler. Fix: give
  `ModelContextProtocol` and `AllToolsets` `"TargetAllowList": ["Editor"]` in the `.uproject`.
  UAT then prints "no longer being treated as a code-based project".
- **A content-only project is packaged without `-build` and without `-target=`.** With
  `-target=UnrealGame`: "Unable to find target 'UnrealGame'". With `-build` and no target:
  "does not look like uproject file but no targets have been found!". The reason is in
  `AutomationUtils/ProjectParams.cs`: with `-build`, UAT wants a `.Target.cs` inside the project.
- **A `"Modules"` key in the `.uproject` makes it a code project, even as `"Modules": []`.** UAT
  tests for the literal text (`ProjectUtils.cs`: `uprojectStr.Contains("\"Modules\"")`). Staging then
  fails with "Missing receipt '...\Binaries\Win64\<Name>.target'". The engine's own `TP_BlankBP`

## SUPERCUT core lane (13 Nov 2026, c4, engine 5.8.4)

All verified on c4 in the project at `D:\UE\Projects\Supercut` unless marked `docs`.

- **A compile can die with `C1001: Internal compiler error` and no source line when memory is
  short** (verified). The first build of a 12-file module failed on most files with
  `c1xx: fatal error C1001 (compiler file 'msc1.cpp', line 1589)`. c4 had 5.9 GB of 31 GB free.
  UBT starts one compile per core and each maps the shared precompiled header. Fix: add
  `-MaxParallelActions=3` to the `Build.bat` line. Through UAT the same switch goes in as
  `-ubtargs=-MaxParallelActions=3`.
- **A local variable named `Player` inside an `APlayerController` subclass breaks the build**
  (verified): `error C4458: declaration of 'Player' hides class member`. The class has a member
  called `Player`, and the engine builds with that warning as an error. Use another name.
- **A clean exit returns 0 on Windows whatever code you ask for** (verified, and read in
  `WindowsPlatformMisc.cpp`). `FPlatformMisc::RequestExitWithStatus(false, 2)` posts the code with
  `PostQuitMessage`, and the launcher's main loop returns its own value. A scripted run that
  logged an error and asked for code 2 came back as 0. With `Force` true the engine flushes the
  log and calls `TerminateProcess` with the code, and the caller sees 2. The engine's own
  automation quit does the same.
- **The first screenshot of a run stalls the game, and the world clock only moves 0.4 s for it**
  (verified, three runs out of three). `FScreenshotRequest::RequestScreenshot` on the first call
  froze the window for longer than 0.4 s. `AWorldSettings::FixupDeltaSeconds` clamps a frame to
  `MaxUndilatedFrameTime`, so game time jumped by exactly 0.40. Later screenshots cost a few
  frames. For a timed script: take one throwaway picture early, and leave 0.3 s between a
  picture and any step whose timing matters.

# Lane feel1: tuning file and practice keys

Game repo `D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59`, branch `ue59`, commit **`3c91247`** on top of `ea7e6eb`. Not pushed.

## For the owner (short enough to paste)

**Change a number without a rebuild.** In the game folder, next to `Supercut.exe`, is `Tuning.example.txt`: every
number in the game with its default and what it does. Make a file called `Tuning.txt` in the same folder and copy
in only the lines you want to change, for example:

```
WalkSpeed = 750
FreezeSeconds = 5
GruntHealth = 4
```

`#` starts a comment. Names must match exactly (capitals count). Whole-number fields such as `Charges` take no
fraction. The game reads the file when it starts. A line it cannot use is not applied, and it is listed in red at the
top left for 8 seconds with its line number. The other lines still apply. While any number differs from its default
the top right says `TUNED: n values`. Delete `Tuning.txt` (or empty it) to go back to the defaults.

**Practice keys.** Start the game with `Play_dev.bat` instead of `Supercut.exe`. Then:

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| F1 | restart the room (charges full, everything reset) |
| F2 | next room, no upgrade pick |
| F3 | room before |
| F4 | no damage on / off (`NO DAMAGE` shows) |
| F5 | read `Tuning.txt` again and restart the room: edit the file, alt-tab back, press F5 |
| F6 | every upgrade / none (`ALL UPGRADES` shows while you hold them all) |
| F9 | show / hide this list in the game |

A plain `Supercut.exe` start has none of these keys.

# Lane feel2: handoff

14 Nov 2026, c4. Game repo `D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59`, branch `ue59`, from `440abca`. Not pushed.

## Commit

- `3583521` SUPERCUT feel2: hit, kill, hurt and board feedback, tuning ranges (34 files).

The running log, with the dead ends, is `LOG.md` beside this file.

## New fields

Every one is `[taste: owner review]`. Off value: what to set in Tuning.txt to turn the effect off. A dash means the
field only shapes an effect, and that effect has its own off switch.

| Field | Default | Off | Range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JumpCutFraction | 0.5 | 1 | 0 to 1 | Letting go of jump while rising cuts the upward speed to this share. Scripted jumps count as held. |

/**
 * The one owner of time: rolling or frozen, the clapperboard charges and the freeze timer.
 *
 * How a freeze works: every actor that belongs to the scene (enemies, their shots, machines) calls
 * JoinScene once. While frozen, each of them has AActor::CustomTimeDilation set to 0. The engine
 * multiplies an actor's tick time, and its components' tick time, by that number, so a frozen actor
 * still ticks but with zero seconds passed. It does not move, its timers do not count, and nothing
 * about it is lost. The player, the gun and the HUD never join, so they run on.
 */

	GENERATED_BODY()

void FAudioDevice::HandlePause(bool bGameTicking, bool bGlobalPause)
{
	DECLARE_CYCLE_STAT(TEXT("FAudioThreadTask.HandlePause"), STAT_AudioHandlePause, STATGROUP_AudioThreadCommands);

	// Run this command on the audio thread if this is getting called on game thread
	if (!IsInAudioThread())
	{
		FAudioDevice* AudioDevice = this;
		FAudioThread::RunCommandOnAudioThread([AudioDevice, bGameTicking, bGlobalPause]()
		{
			AudioDevice->HandlePause(bGameTicking, bGlobalPause);
		}, GET_STATID(STAT_AudioHandlePause));

		return;
	}

	// Handles the global pause/unpause feature

	// Pause all sounds if transitioning to pause mode.
	if (!bGameTicking && (bGameWasTicking || bGlobalPause))
	{
		for (int32 i = 0; i < Sources.Num(); i++)
		{
			FSoundSource* Source = Sources[ i ];
			if (!Source->IsPausedByGame() && (bGlobalPause || Source->IsGameOnly()))
			{
				Source->SetPauseByGame(true);
			}
		}
	}
	// Unpause all sounds if transitioning back to game.
	else if (bGameTicking && (!bGameWasTicking || bGlobalPause))
	{
		for (int32 i = 0; i < Sources.Num(); i++)
		{
			FSoundSource* Source = Sources[ i ];
			if (Source->IsPausedByGame() && (bGlobalPause || Source->IsGameOnly()))
			{
				Source->SetPauseByGame(false);
			}
		}
	}

	bGameWasTicking = bGameTicking;
}

	UpdateCameraKicks(DeltaSeconds);

/** The game module. Its one job of its own: "-SupercutWriteTuning" writes Tuning.example.txt and quits before a window opens. */
class FSupercutModule : public FDefaultGameModuleImpl
{
public:
	virtual void StartupModule() override
	{
		if (!FParse::Param(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("SupercutWriteTuning")))
		{
			return;
		}
		const FString Path = SupercutTuningFile::TemplatePath();
		const bool bWritten = FFileHelper::SaveStringToFile(SupercutTuningFile::WriteTemplate(FSupercutTuning()), *Path);
		if (bWritten)
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("TUNING template written to %s"), *Path);
		}
		else
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Error, TEXT("TUNING template could not be written to %s"), *Path);
		}
		// Force: leave now, before the engine opens a window. The log is flushed first (WindowsPlatformMisc.cpp).
		FPlatformMisc::RequestExitWithStatus(true, bWritten ? 0 : 1);
	}
};

/**
 * Tuning.txt: the numbers of FSupercutTuning, changed without a rebuild.
 *
 * The file holds one "Name = value" per line; # starts a comment, blank lines are skipped. Names are the struct's
 * field names. It is read when the game starts (ASupercutGameMode::InitGame) and again on the practice key F5.
 * Each read starts from the struct's defaults, so a line taken out of the file goes back to its default.
 * With no file every number is its default.
 *
 * A bad line (no "=", an unknown name, a value that is not a number, a number with a fraction for a whole-number
 * field, a value outside the field's range, a name given twice) is not applied. It is listed in the log and drawn
 * in red by the HUD; the good lines still apply. The game goes on: a person edits this file by hand.
 *
 * The file sits next to Supercut.exe: in a packaged build the folder that holds Supercut.exe, Engine and
 * Supercut (FPaths::RootDir); in an editor build the project folder.
 * "Supercut.exe -SupercutWriteTuning" writes Tuning.example.txt there, every field with its default and the
 * header's comment, and quits.
 */

		double Lowest;                           // the lowest value Tuning.txt may set; a value outside is a bad line
		double Highest;                          // the highest

	void Load(const FString& Path)
	{
		FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
		Tuning = FSupercutTuning();
		Problems.Reset();
		FileName = FPaths::GetCleanFilename(Path);
		++Loads;

		if (!IFileManager::Get().FileExists(*Path))
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("TUNING no file at %s: every number is its default"), *Path);
			return;
		}
		TArray<FString> Lines;
		if (!FFileHelper::LoadFileToStringArray(Lines, *Path))
		{
			Problems.Add({ 0, TEXT("the file is there but cannot be read, so every number is its default.") });
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Warning, TEXT("TUNING %s cannot be read: every number is its default"), *Path);
			return;
		}
		const FReadResult Result = Parse(Lines, Tuning);
		Problems = Result.Problems;
		for (const FProblem& Problem : Problems)
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Warning, TEXT("TUNING bad line %s line %d: %s Not applied."), *FileName, Problem.Line, *Problem.Text);
		}
		TArray<FString> Changes;
		const FSupercutTuning Defaults;
		for (const FString& Name : ChangedNames(Tuning))
		{
			const FEntry* Entry = Entries().FindByPredicate([&Name](const FEntry& E) { return Name == E.Name; });
			Changes.Add(FString::Printf(TEXT("%s %s -> %s"), *Name, *ValueText(*Entry, Defaults), *ValueText(*Entry, Tuning)));
		}
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("TUNING read %s: %d lines applied, %d bad, %d values differ from the defaults%s%s"),
			*Path, Result.Applied, Problems.Num(), Changes.Num(), Changes.Num() ? TEXT(": ") : TEXT(""), *FString::Join(Changes, TEXT(", ")));
	}

	const TArray<FProblem>& LastProblems()
	{
		return Problems;
	}

	FString LastFileName()
	{
		return FileName;
	}

	int32 LoadCount()
	{
		return Loads;
	}
}

# Makes the project's content assets: one empty map, the surface materials (M_Solid, M_Glow and its halo M_Halo), the frozen-time sketch, the
# tabletop model's surfaces (M_Maquette) and the dark studio round the model (M_Studio).
# The game builds everything else in C++ at run time.
#
# Run headless from the project folder:
#   D:\UE\UE_5.9\Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59\Supercut.uproject
#     -run=pythonscript -Script=D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59\Tools\make_assets.py -AllowCommandletRendering -unattended -nopause -nosplash
#   (-nullrhi does not work: with no renderer the material editing library refuses to compile a material.)
#
# Safe to run again: it replaces what it made.

import os

import unreal

MEL = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary
EAL = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary
TOOLS = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()
PROJECT = unreal.Paths.convert_relative_path_to_full(unreal.Paths.project_dir())


def collection_param(material, collection, name, y):
    node = MEL.create_material_expression(material, unreal.MaterialExpressionCollectionParameter, -500, y)
    node.set_editor_property("collection", collection)
    node.set_editor_property("parameter_name", name)
    return node


def make_glow(collection):
    # An unlit, self-lit surface: Color times Strength. In frozen time the strength falls to FrozenGlow: a bright glow
    # tonemaps to near white and loses its hue, and the sketch keeps a signal's live colour.
    material = fresh("M_Glow", "/Game/Materials", unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew())
    material.set_editor_property("shading_model", unreal.MaterialShadingModel.MSM_UNLIT)
    color = vector_param(material, "Color", (1.0, 1.0, 1.0), 0)
    strength = scalar_param(material, "Strength", 1.0, 200)
    lerp = MEL.create_material_expression(material, unreal.MaterialExpressionLinearInterpolate, -300, 300)
    for node, pin in ((strength, "A"), (collection_param(material, collection, "FrozenGlow", 400), "B"),
                      (collection_param(material, collection, "Blend", 500), "Alpha")):

FQualityLevels BenchmarkQualityLevels(uint32 WorkScale, float CPUMultiplier, float GPUMultiplier)
{
	ensure((CPUMultiplier > 0.0f) && (GPUMultiplier > 0.0f));

	// benchmark the system

	TArray<float> CPUBenchmarkSteps;
	TArray<float> GPUBenchmarkSteps;

	FSynthBenchmarkResults SynthBenchmark;
	ISynthBenchmark::Get().Run(SynthBenchmark, true, WorkScale);

	float CPUPerfIndex = SynthBenchmark.ComputeCPUPerfIndex(/*out*/ &CPUBenchmarkSteps) * CPUMultiplier;
	float GPUPerfIndex = SynthBenchmark.ComputeGPUPerfIndex(/*out*/ &GPUBenchmarkSteps) * GPUMultiplier;

#if !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING
	if (CVarTestCPUPerfIndexOverride.GetValueOnAnyThread() > 0.0f)
	{
		CPUPerfIndex = CVarTestCPUPerfIndexOverride.GetValueOnAnyThread();
	}
	if (CVarTestGPUPerfIndexOverride.GetValueOnAnyThread() > 0.0f)
	{
		GPUPerfIndex = CVarTestGPUPerfIndexOverride.GetValueOnAnyThread();
	}
#endif

	// decide on the actual quality needed
	FQualityLevels Results = ComputeQualityLevelsFromPerfIndex(CPUPerfIndex, GPUPerfIndex);
	Results.CPUBenchmarkSteps = MoveTemp(CPUBenchmarkSteps);
	Results.GPUBenchmarkSteps = MoveTemp(GPUBenchmarkSteps);

	return Results;
}

static void PrintGroupInfo(const TCHAR* InGroupName, bool bInInfoMode)
{
	int32 QualityLevel = -1;
	TArray<FString> CVars;

	if (bInInfoMode)

		if (QualityLevel != -1)

			for (int32 CVarDataIndex = 0; CVarDataIndex < CVars.Num(); ++CVarDataIndex)
			{
				UE_LOGF(LogConsoleResponse, Display, "    %ls", *CVars[CVarDataIndex]);
			}
		}
	}
}

	// The default module's render mode comes from the command line. Both flags select the non-realtime renderer.
	Audio::EDeviceRenderMode GetDefaultRenderModeFromCommandLine()
	{
		if (FParse::Param(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("DeterministicAudio")))
		{
			return Audio::EDeviceRenderMode::Deterministic;
		}
		if (FParse::Param(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("NonRealtimeAudio")))
		{
			return Audio::EDeviceRenderMode::NonRealtime;
		}
		return Audio::EDeviceRenderMode::Realtime;
	}

		bool Start(bool bController = false)

			{
				return false;
			}
			GetTestWorld()->GetWorldSettings()->DefaultGameMode = AGameModeBase::StaticClass();
			if (!BeginPlayInTestWorld())
			{

			{

				// No local player in a test world, so the engine would treat it as remote: the character would not
				// move and the camera would not follow the control rotation.
				Controller->SetAsLocalPlayerController();
			}
			return true;
		}

		void Step()
		{
			TickTestWorld(FeelTestStep);
		}

		{
			const int32 Ticks = FMath::RoundToInt(Seconds / FeelTestStep);
			for (int32 Tick = 0; Tick < Ticks; ++Tick)
			{
				Step();
			}
		}

void ASupercutCharacter::ApplyTuning()
{
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	UCharacterMovementComponent* Move = GetCharacterMovement();
	Move->MaxWalkSpeed = Tuning.WalkSpeed;
	Move->GravityScale = Tuning.GravityScale;
	// Launch speed that reaches the apex under this gravity: v = sqrt(2 g h).
	Move->JumpZVelocity = FMath::Sqrt(2.f * FMath::Abs(GetWorld()->GetGravityZ()) * Tuning.GravityScale * Tuning.JumpApex);
	Move->AirControl = Tuning.AirControl;
	Move->MaxAcceleration = Tuning.GroundAcceleration;
	Move->BrakingDecelerationWalking = Tuning.GroundBraking;
	Move->GroundFriction = Tuning.GroundFriction;

**Sat 14 Nov 05:11:10 · Tool call: Bash** (Append design notes to lane log)

L="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/shell1"; cat >> "$L/LOG.md" <<'EOF'
- Free memory 13.4 GB at start.

## Step 1: engine facts read in the 5.9 source (before any code)

- Shipping cannot log through the engine here. `bUseLoggingInShipping` is `[RequiresUniqueBuildEnvironment]`
  (UBT TargetRules.cs:1708) and an installed engine refuses a unique build environment (RulesAssembly.cs:719).
  With `NO_LOGGING`, `UE_LOG` compiles to nothing but the Fatal branch (LogMacros.h:184). So `-log` and `-abslog=`
  cannot help. Plan: in Shipping only, the game module redefines `UE_LOG` to write its lines to a file named by
  `-SupercutLog=<file>`.
- Shipping parses `-UseFixedTimeStep` (WITH_FIXED_TIME_STEP_SUPPORT is on by default) but not `-FPS=`
  (LaunchEngineLoop.cpp InitTime, inside `#if !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING`). The fixed step would be the default 1/30 s.
  Plan: the game module reads `-FPS=` itself in Shipping.
- `-DeterministicAudio` is parsed in every build (AudioDeviceManager.cpp:113), so `-Silent` stays silent in Shipping.
- Shipping on desktop counts as installed (App.cpp:219), so its Saved folder is the user's:
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Supercut\Saved\` (Paths.cpp ShouldSaveToUserDir / ProjectSavedDir). To be checked by a run.
- A paused world stops every non-UI sound source (AudioDevice.cpp HandlePause, called with bGameTicking false
  from GameEngine.cpp:2099 when no world is unpaused). UI sounds (bIsUISound) play on: here that is the music
  synth and the ui_* cues. So the pause menu pauses scene sounds by itself through SetPause.
- The game's script switches were inside `#if !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING` (controller BeginPlay, game mode InitGame).
  They have to parse in Shipping for E4.

## Step 1 design

- `USupercutUserSettings` (UGameUserSettings subclass, named in DefaultEngine.ini): Sensitivity, Volume and a
  bQualityChosen flag as config fields; quality = engine overall scalability level; display = window mode.
  Setters only set values; `ApplyAndSave` applies (window only when DISPLAY changed, so a scripted run's
  -ResX is not overridden) and saves.
- `USupercutMenu` world subsystem: the screen (title, pause, settings, controls), its rows, the chosen row, key and
  click handling, pause and resume. The controller only feeds it keys and clicks, so tests drive it directly.
- Title: `USupercutRun` gets a Title phase. Room 1 is built with no sound, the character holds the sketch look
  (`ShowTitleLook`), the world is paused. START runs a fresh take from scene 1, as a plain start did.
- `-SupercutTitle`: shows the title even with a script, for the scripted title checks.
- Halo fade: per pixel in `M_Halo` (camera distance from PixelDepth), because the Marksman's line ends at the
  player and a per-object fade would remove its whole halo.
EOF

USupercutRun& USupercutRun::Get(const UObject* WorldContext)
{
	check(WorldContext);
	UWorld* World = WorldContext->GetWorld();
	checkf(World, TEXT("USupercutRun::Get: %s has no world"), *WorldContext->GetName());
	USupercutRun* Run = World->GetSubsystem<USupercutRun>();
	checkf(Run, TEXT("USupercutRun::Get: world %s has no run"), *World->GetName());
	return *Run;
}

void USupercutRun::Initialize(FSubsystemCollectionBase& Collection)
{
	Super::Initialize(Collection);
	USupercutTime* Time = Collection.InitializeDependency<USupercutTime>();
	check(Time);
	Time->OnFroze.AddUObject(this, &USupercutRun::OnFroze);
}

{
	return float(GetWorld()->GetRealTimeSeconds() - PhaseSince);
}

float USupercutRun::GetSecondsInRoom() const
{
	return float(GetWorld()->GetRealTimeSeconds() - RoomSince);
}

void USupercutRun::SetPhase(ESupercutRunPhase NewPhase)
{
	Phase = NewPhase;
	PhaseSince = GetWorld()->GetRealTimeSeconds();
}

}

void USupercutRun::NextRun()
{
	checkf(Phase == ESupercutRunPhase::Wrapped, TEXT("USupercutRun::NextRun: the run has not wrapped"));
	SetPaused(false);
	Take = 1;
	Stats = FSupercutRunStats();
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("RUN begins again"));
	StartTake();
}

void USupercutRun::PracticeEnterRoom(int32 Index)
{
	checkf(Phase == ESupercutRunPhase::Playing || Phase == ESupercutRunPhase::Picking, TEXT("USupercutRun::PracticeEnterRoom: not in a room or on the upgrade screen"));
	checkf(RoomNames.IsValidIndex(Index), TEXT("USupercutRun::PracticeEnterRoom: the run has no scene %d"), Index + 1);
	if (Phase == ESupercutRunPhase::Picking)
	{
		Offer.Reset();
		SetPaused(false);
	}
	EnterRoom(Index, false);
}

void USupercutRun::PracticeHoldAllUpgrades(bool bAll)
{
	if (bAll)
	{
		for (const FSupercutUpgrade& Upgrade : SupercutUpgrades::All())
		{
			if (!Held.Contains(Upgrade.Key))
			{
				Grant(Upgrade.Key);
			}
		}
	}
	else
	{
		Held.Reset();
		SupercutUpgrades::ApplyRules(*this);
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("UPGRADE all taken away (0 held)"));
	}
}

void USupercutRun::Tick(float DeltaTime)
{
	Super::Tick(DeltaTime);
	if (Phase == ESupercutRunPhase::Idle)
	{
		return;
	}

	// The first of these frames holds the room change itself. The frame after it is the first to draw the new room.
	if (bLogFrames)
	{
		FramesAfterChange.Add(float(FApp::GetDeltaTime()) * 1000.f);
		if (FramesAfterChange.Num() == FramesLoggedAfterChange)
		{
			bLogFrames = false;
			TArray<FString> Times;
			for (const float Frame : FramesAfterChange)
			{
				Times.Add(FString::Printf(TEXT("%.1f"), Frame));
			}
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("ROOM change frames: the %d frames from the change took %s ms"), FramesLoggedAfterChange, *FString::Join(Times, TEXT(", ")));
		}
	}

	if (Phase == ESupercutRunPhase::Playing)
	{
		Stats.Seconds += DeltaTime;
		if (Hero->IsDead())
		{
			SetPhase(ESupercutRunPhase::Dead);
			DeadFor = 0.f;
			USupercutAudio::Get(this).MusicStop();   // the reel ran out: the music goes with it
		}
		else if (Room->IsGateReached())
		{
			ReachGate();
		}
	}
	else if (Phase == ESupercutRunPhase::Dead)
	{
		DeadFor += DeltaTime;
		if (DeadFor >= FSupercutTuning::Get().DeathRestartDelay)
		{
			++Take;
			StartTake();
		}
	}
}

{
	// The upgrade and wrap screens pause the game. PlayerTick has to run there, to read the keys and to keep a script going.

void ASupercutPlayerController::BeginPlay()
{
	Super::BeginPlay();
	RoomEntriesSeen = USupercutRun::Get(this).GetRoomEntries();

#if !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING
	FString ScriptPath;
	if (FParse::Value(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("-SupercutScript="), ScriptPath))
	{
		LoadScript(ScriptPath);
	}
	if (FParse::Value(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("-SupercutShots="), ShotFolder))
	{
		IFileManager::Get().MakeDirectory(*ShotFolder, true);
	}
	bCountFps = FParse::Param(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("SupercutFps"));
	bQuitAtEnd = FParse::Param(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("SupercutQuit"));
	bTrace = FParse::Param(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("SupercutTrace"));
#endif

	if (!bScripted)
	{
		// A person is playing: the game takes the mouse. A run started with a script never does,
		// so it cannot grab the mouse of whoever is at the PC.
		SetInputMode(FInputModeGameOnly());
		bShowMouseCursor = false;
	}
}

void UGameUserSettings::LoadSettings(bool bForceReload/*=false*/)
{
	QUICK_SCOPE_CYCLE_COUNTER(GameUserSettings_LoadSettings);

	if (bForceReload)
	{
        if (OnUpdateGameUserSettingsFileFromCloud.IsBound())
        {
            FString IniFileLocation = FPaths::GeneratedConfigDir() + UGameplayStatics::GetPlatformName() + "/" +  GGameUserSettingsIni + ".ini";
            UE_LOGF(LogGameUserSettings, Verbose, "%ls", *IniFileLocation);

            if (!OnUpdateGameUserSettingsFileFromCloud.Execute(FString(*IniFileLocation)))
            {
                UE_LOGF(LogGameUserSettings, Warning, "Failed to read the ini file from the Cloud interface %ls", *IniFileLocation);
            }
        }
        
		LoadConfigIni(bForceReload);
	}
	LoadConfig(GetClass(), *GGameUserSettingsIni);

	// Note: Scalability::LoadState() should not be needed as we already loaded the settings earlier (needed so the engine can startup with that before the game is initialized)
	ScalabilityQuality = Scalability::GetQualityLevels();

	// Allow override using command-line settings
	bool bDetectingResolution = ResolutionSizeX == 0 || ResolutionSizeY == 0;

	if (bDetectingResolution)
	{
		ConfirmVideoMode();
	}

	// Update r.FullScreenMode CVar
	SetPreferredFullscreenMode(PreferredFullscreenMode);

	// Window position backwards compatability
	PRAGMA_DISABLE_DEPRECATION_WARNINGS
	const FIntPoint OldWindowPosition(WindowPosX_DEPRECATED, WindowPosY_DEPRECATED);
	PRAGMA_ENABLE_DEPRECATION_WARNINGS

	if (OldWindowPosition != GetDefaultWindowPosition())
	{
		if (WindowPositions.IsEmpty())
		{
			WindowPositions.SetNum(1);
		}
		WindowPositions[0] = OldWindowPosition;

		// Write out the non-deprecated value
		SaveConfig(CPF_Config, *GGameUserSettingsIni);
	}
}

void UGameUserSettings::RequestResolutionChange(int32 InResolutionX, int32 InResolutionY, EWindowMode::Type InWindowMode, bool bInDoOverrides /* = true */, int32 MonitorIndex /* = -1 */)
{
	if (FPlatformProperties::HasFixedResolution())
	{
		return;
	}

	if (bInDoOverrides)
	{
		UGameEngine::ConditionallyOverrideSettings(InResolutionX, InResolutionY, InWindowMode, MonitorIndex);
	}

	FSystemResolution::SetMonitorIndex(MonitorIndex);
	FSystemResolution::RequestResolutionChange(InResolutionX, InResolutionY, InWindowMode);
}

bool FSupercutFeelHoldFreezeTest::RunTest(const FString& Parameters)
{

	{
		return false;
	}
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	USupercutTime& Time = World.Time();
	ASupercutGrunt* Hit = World.Spawn<ASupercutGrunt>(FVector(0.f, 0.f, 0.f));
	ASupercutGrunt* Other = World.Spawn<ASupercutGrunt>(FVector(0.f, 500.f, 0.f));
	Hit->bPassive = true;
	Other->bPassive = true;
	World.Run(0.1f);

	// A hit while rolling: this enemy's clock stops, nobody else's.
	Hit->TakeHit(1, FVector(1.f, 0.f, 0.f));
	TestTrue(TEXT("the hit enemy is held"), Time.IsHeld(Hit));
	TestEqual(TEXT("its clock is stopped"), Hit->CustomTimeDilation, 0.f);
	TestEqual(TEXT("the other enemy runs on"), Other->CustomTimeDilation, 1.f);
	TestFalse(TEXT("no freeze"), Time.IsFrozen());

	// A freeze catches the hold part way: the enemy never runs during the freeze.
	World.Run(0.03f);
	TestTrue(TEXT("still held 0.03 s in"), Time.IsHeld(Hit));
	const float ClipAt = Hit->GetFigure()->GetPosition();
	Time.PressClapper();
	bool bRanInFreeze = false;
	for (int32 Tick = 0; Tick < 100; ++Tick)

		World.Step();
		bRanInFreeze |= Hit->CustomTimeDilation != 0.f || Other->CustomTimeDilation != 0.f;
	}

	TestEqual(TEXT("the held enemy's clip did not move in the freeze"), Hit->GetFigure()->GetPosition(), ClipAt);

import sys
def edit(path, pairs):
    s = open(path, newline='', encoding='utf-8').read()
    crlf = '\r\n' in s
    s = s.replace('\r\n', '\n')
    for a, b in pairs:
        n = s.count(a)
        if n != 1:
            raise SystemExit('%s: %d matches for:\n%s' % (path, n, a))
        s = s.replace(a, b)
    if crlf:
        s = s.replace('\n', '\r\n')
    open(path, 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
    print('edited', path, 'crlf' if crlf else 'lf', len(pairs))

void USupercutRun::StartFromTitle()
{

	SetPaused(false);
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("RUN begins: %d rooms (%s), seed %d"), RoomNames.Num(), *FString::Join(RoomNames, TEXT(", ")), RunSeed);

void USupercutRun::RestartRun()
{

	StartOver(TEXT("RUN restarts"), true);
}

void USupercutRun::StartOver(const TCHAR* Why, bool bFreshOffers)
{
	SetPaused(false);
	Offer.Reset();
	if (bFreshOffers)
	{
		Random.Initialize(RunSeed);
	}
	Take = 1;
	Stats = FSupercutRunStats();
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("%s"), Why);
	StartTake();
}

	Stats = FSupercutRunStats();

// Holds the camera's sub-pixel jitter still while the sketch is on. The sketch reads depth and normals, which are
// jittered each frame and drawn after TSR has smoothed the picture, so with jitter its lines crawl on a still camera.
class FSupercutStillFrame : public FWorldSceneViewExtension
{
public:
	FSupercutStillFrame(const FAutoRegister& AutoRegister, UWorld* World) : FWorldSceneViewExtension(AutoRegister, World) {}
	bool bStill = false;

	virtual void SetupView(FSceneViewFamily& ViewFamily, FSceneView& View) override
	{
		if (bStill)
		{
			View.bAllowTemporalJitter = false;
		}
	}
};

void ASupercutCharacter::ShowTitleLook()
{
	bTitleLook = true;
	if (!HasActorBegunPlay())
	{
		return;   // BeginPlay calls this again once the sketch exists
	}
	// The title screen pauses the game, so Tick does not run there: the look is set here in full.
	SketchBlend = 1.f;
	Sketch->SetScalarParameterValue(TEXT("Blend"), 1.f);
	SketchValues->SetScalarParameterValue(TEXT("Blend"), 1.f);
	StillFrame->bStill = true;
	Camera->AddOrUpdateBlendable(Sketch, 1.f);
	GunRoot->SetVisibility(false, true);
	ClapRoot->SetVisibility(false, true);
}

FBox2D ASupercutHUD::CardRect(int32 Index, int32 Count, float W, float H)
{
	// Cards are rows, one under the other, so a card's one line of text has the width of the screen to sit in.
	const float S = H / 720.f;
	const float CardW = 1000.f * S;
	const float CardH = 112.f * S;
	const float Gap = 20.f * S;
	const float Top = H * 0.5f - (Count * CardH + (Count - 1) * Gap) * 0.5f;
	const FVector2D Corner(W * 0.5f - CardW * 0.5f, Top + Index * (CardH + Gap));
	return FBox2D(Corner, Corner + FVector2D(CardW, CardH));
}

void ASupercutHUD::DrawUpgradeScreen(const USupercutRun& Run, float W, float H, float S)

	const FLinearColor White(1.f, 1.f, 1.f, 0.92f);

FBox2D ASupercutHUD::MenuRowRect(ESupercutScreen Screen, int32 Index, int32 Count, float W, float H)
{
	const float S = H / 720.f;
	const float RowW = (Screen == ESupercutScreen::Settings ? 560.f : 400.f) * S;
	const float RowH = 46.f * S;
	float Top = H * 0.36f;
	if (Screen == ESupercutScreen::Title)
	{
		Top = H * 0.52f;
	}
	else if (Screen == ESupercutScreen::Controls)
	{
		Top = H * 0.32f + USupercutMenu::ControlLines().Num() * 34.f * S + 24.f * S;
	}
	const FVector2D Corner(W * 0.5f - RowW * 0.5f, Top + Index * RowH);
	return FBox2D(Corner, Corner + FVector2D(RowW, RowH));
}

void ASupercutPlayerController::RunScript(float DeltaTime, FSupercutInput& Input, ASupercutCharacter* Hero, USupercutRun& Run)
{
	if (bScriptOver)
	{
		return;
	}

	if (Hero->IsDead() && !bDeathExpected)
	{
		FailScript(FString::Printf(TEXT("the player died (%s)"), *Hero->GetDeathCause()));
		return;
	}

	ScriptClock += DeltaTime;
	while (NextStep < Steps.Num() && Steps[NextStep].Time <= ScriptClock)
	{
		const FStep& Step = Steps[NextStep];
		if (Step.Command == TEXT("scene"))
		{
			if (Run.GetRoomEntries() == RoomEntriesSeen)
			{
				// Still in the old room, or on a screen between rooms. Wait here.
				SceneWait += DeltaTime;
				if (SceneWait > SceneWaitLimit)
				{
					FailScript(FString::Printf(TEXT("waited %.0f s at a \"scene\" line and the run did not enter a new room"), SceneWaitLimit));
					return;
				}
				break;
			}
			const int32 WantScene = Step.Args.IsValidIndex(0) ? FCString::Atoi(*Step.Args[0]) : 0;
			const int32 WantTake = Step.Args.IsValidIndex(1) ? FCString::Atoi(*Step.Args[1]) : Run.GetTake();
			if (WantScene != Run.GetScene() || WantTake != Run.GetTake())
			{
				FailScript(FString::Printf(TEXT("the script expected scene %d take %d and the run is in scene %d take %d"), WantScene, WantTake, Run.GetScene(), Run.GetTake()));
				return;
			}
			RoomEntriesSeen = Run.GetRoomEntries();
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("SCRIPT scene %d take %d entered after %.2f s, clock set to 0"), Run.GetScene(), Run.GetTake(), ScriptClock);
			ScriptClock = 0.f;
			SceneWait = 0.f;
			HeldForward = 0.f;
			HeldRight = 0.f;
			bHeldFire = false;
			bDeathExpected = false;
			++NextStep;
			continue;
		}

		RunStep(Step, Input, Hero);
		++NextStep;
		if (bScriptOver)
		{
			return;
		}
	}
	Input.Forward = HeldForward;
	Input.Right = HeldRight;
	Input.bFire = Input.bFire || bHeldFire;
}

void ASupercutPlayerController::LookAt(const FVector& Point, ASupercutCharacter* Hero)
{
	SetControlRotation((Point - Hero->GetEyeLocation()).Rotation());
}

/** The game module. Its one job of its own: "-SupercutWriteTuning" writes Tuning.example.txt and quits before a window opens. */
class FSupercutModule : public FDefaultGameModuleImpl
{
public:
	virtual void StartupModule() override
	{
		if (!FParse::Param(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("SupercutWriteTuning")))
		{
			return;
		}
		const FString Path = SupercutTuningFile::TemplatePath();
		const bool bWritten = FFileHelper::SaveStringToFile(SupercutTuningFile::WriteTemplate(FSupercutTuning()), *Path);
		if (bWritten)
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("TUNING template written to %s"), *Path);
		}
		else
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Error, TEXT("TUNING template could not be written to %s"), *Path);
		}
		// Force: leave now, before the engine opens a window. The log is flushed first (WindowsPlatformMisc.cpp).
		FPlatformMisc::RequestExitWithStatus(true, bWritten ? 0 : 1);
	}
};

IMPLEMENT_PRIMARY_GAME_MODULE(FSupercutModule, Supercut, "Supercut");

UMaterialInstanceDynamic* SupercutShapes::AddHalo(AActor* Owner, UStaticMeshComponent* GlowPart, ESupercutShape Shape, const FVector& Across, const FLinearColor& Color)
{
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	UMaterialInterface* Base = LoadOrDie<UMaterialInterface>(TEXT("/Game/Materials/M_Halo.M_Halo"));
	UMaterialInstanceDynamic* Material = UMaterialInstanceDynamic::Create(Base, Owner);
	Material->SetVectorParameterValue(TEXT("Color"), Color);
	Material->SetScalarParameterValue(TEXT("Opacity"), Tuning.HaloOpacity);
	// The part's own size is 100 cm in its own space, so this size is a scale on top of the part's.
	const FVector Size = (FVector::OneVector + Across * (Tuning.HaloSize - 1.f)) * 100.0;
	UStaticMeshComponent* Shell = Add(Owner, GlowPart, Shape, FVector::ZeroVector, FRotator::ZeroRotator, Size, Material);
	Shell->SetCastShadow(false);
	return Material;
}

	int32 TuningFieldCount()

	{
		TArray<FString> Lines;

		return Lines;
	}

	FString TuningTestFile(const TCHAR* Name, const TArray<FString>& Lines)
	{
		const FString Path = FPaths::ConvertRelativePathToFull(FPaths::Combine(FPaths::ProjectSavedDir(), TEXT("TuningTests"), Name));
		FFileHelper::SaveStringToFile(FString::Join(Lines, TEXT("\r\n")), *Path);
		return Path;

## SUPERCUT slice lane (13 Nov 2026, c4, engine 5.9 preview)

- **The material editing library will not compile under `-nullrhi`** (13 Nov 2026, verified). A Python commandlet run
  with `-nullrhi` fails with "Cannot compile material ... no renderer", after `fresh()` has already deleted the old
  asset. Run make_assets with `-AllowCommandletRendering` instead; it stays headless. `recompile_material` only queues
  the compile there: the shaders really compile in the package cook, so read `package_run.log` for material errors.
- **A post-process material after tonemapping reads jittered depth and normals** (13 Nov 2026, verified). TSR has

- **`PreSkinnedNormal` is vertex-shader only** (13 Nov 2026, verified). Wired into a Custom node that feeds Base Colour,

- `USupercutUserSettings` (UGameUserSettings subclass, named in DefaultEngine.ini): Sensitivity, Volume and a
  bQualityChosen flag as config fields; quality = engine overall scalability level; display = window mode.
  Setters only set values; `ApplyAndSave` applies (window only when DISPLAY changed, so a scripted run's
  -ResX is not overridden) and saves.
- `USupercutMenu` world subsystem: the screen (title, pause, settings, controls), its rows, the chosen row, key and
  click handling, pause and resume. The controller only feeds it keys and clicks, so tests drive it directly.
- Title: `USupercutRun` gets a Title phase. Room 1 is built with no sound, the character holds the sketch look
  (`ShowTitleLook`), the world is paused. START runs a fresh take from scene 1, as a plain start did.
- `-SupercutTitle`: shows the title even with a script, for the scripted title checks.
- Halo fade: per pixel in `M_Halo` (camera distance from PixelDepth), because the Marksman's line ends at the
  player and a per-object fade would remove its whole halo.
```

```
@echo off
rem Packages the Windows Shipping build with UE 5.9 to D:\UE\Builds\Supercut59_ship. The log goes to Saved\Logs\package_ship_run.log.
rem This is the build for other people: no Tuning.txt is read, no practice keys, no Tuning.example.txt or Play_dev.bat,
rem no .pdb files and no staging manifests. The Development package (Tools\package.cmd) is not touched.
rem Shipping keeps its saved settings under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Supercut\Saved, never in this folder.
rem Its folder is emptied first: the archive step adds files and never removes old ones.
rem The -ubtargs value holds spaces, so it is quoted as one argument. Typed into PowerShell or bash the quotes get lost: run this file.
rem Usage: cmd /c Tools\package_shipping.cmd
set PROJ=%~dp0..
set ARCHIVE=D:\UE\Builds\Supercut59_ship
set OUT=%ARCHIVE%\Windows
if exist "%OUT%" rmdir /s /q "%OUT%"
if exist "%OUT%" (
  echo %OUT% could not be emptied: is the game running from it?
  exit /b 1
)
cd /d D:\UE
call D:\UE\UE_5.9\Engine\Build\BatchFiles\RunUAT.bat BuildCookRun -nop4 -utf8output -unattended -nocompileuat -cook -build -project=%PROJ%\Supercut.uproject -unrealexe=D:\UE\UE_5.9\Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe -platform=Win64 -installed -stage -archive -package -pak -iostore -compressed -nodebuginfo -applocaldirectory=D:\UE\UE_5.9\Engine\Binaries\ThirdParty\AppLocalDependencies -archivedirectory=%ARCHIVE% -clientconfig=Shipping "-ubtargs=-MaxParallelActions=1 -NoHotReloadFromIDE -Log=%PROJ%\Saved\Logs\ubt_package_ship.log" > "%PROJ%\Saved\Logs\package_ship_run.log" 2>&1
if errorlevel 1 exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%
rem The staging step writes its file lists beside the game. They name build paths on this PC and the game never reads them.
del /q "%OUT%\Manifest_*.txt" 2> nul
for /r "%OUT%" %%F in (*.pdb) do del /q "%%F"
for %%N in (Tuning.txt Tuning.example.txt Play_dev.bat) do if exist "%OUT%\%%N" (
  echo %OUT%\%%N should not be in the Shipping folder
  exit /b 1
)
if exist "%OUT%\Supercut\Saved" (
  echo %OUT%\Supercut\Saved should not be in the Shipping folder
  exit /b 1
)
exit /b 0

# Unreal gotchas

Traps and their fixes. Each entry: date, `verified` (we ran it) or `docs` (read, not run), source.
Format and rules: `AGENTS.md` in this folder. Engine in use: 5.8.4 at `D:\UE\UE_5.8`.

## Unreal MCP in 5.8.4 differs from Epic's docs page

All verified 12 Nov 2026 on c4 against the installed engine and a live editor.

- **The plugin is off by default.** `ModelContextProtocol.uplugin` has `EnabledByDefault: false`
  (the docs say it is on). Enable `ModelContextProtocol` and `AllToolsets` in the `.uproject`.
- **The server does not start by itself.** `bAutoStartServer` defaults to `false` in
...
  squared, so the number stays the lux at the middle of the room whatever the room's size.
- **`DestroyComponent` leaves attached children alive** (14 Nov 2026, verified). Destroying a mesh that has a halo
  shell attached left the shell in the world. Destroy the children first. For the same reason `SetVisibility(false)`
  hides only the part itself: pass `true` as the second argument to hide what is attached to it.
- **The sketch counts a stencil value only where custom depth is within 2 cm of scene depth** (14 Nov 2026,
  verified). A flat part placed 2 cm in front of another part with a different stencil value sits on the edge of
  that test and can take the other part's look. Keep such parts 5 cm or more apart.
- **Packaging leaves an old `Tuning.txt` in the build folder** (14 Nov 2026, verified). `Tools\package.cmd` says so
  in a comment. A proof run on a new package still reads the old numbers unless the file is deleted first.
- **Green and red `lamp` lines in room files light the walls near them** (14 Nov 2026, verified). The wall round the
  gate measured about 90 percent brightness whatever the desk lamp did, until `AccentLampScale` halved those lamps.
- **`make_assets.py` gives the sketch collection new parameter ids on every run** (14 Nov 2026, verified, adds to
  the slice2 entry). `MPC_Sketch`, `M_Glow` and `M_Halo` all reference it, so the three must be committed from the
  same asset run. `M_SketchFreeze` and `M_Studio` do not reference it.

- **Pause menu:** Esc in a room or on the death, upgrade or wrap screen opens it and never quits the program. The world stops fully, a freeze included: in a packaged run a freeze paused for 3.5 s still ended at `held 4.00 s`.
- **Settings:** sensitivity, volume, quality and display apply at once, save, and are read back at the next start. In Shipping, volume 50 came back after a restart.
- **Controls screen:** checked against the controller code.
- **Shipping:** `Tools\package_shipping.cmd` builds it. The folder has no tuning files, `.pdb`, manifests or saved settings. Shipping ignores `Tuning.txt` and `-SupercutDev`, which still work in Development.
- **Halo:** fades out between 300 cm and 120 cm from the camera, set by two new tuning fields. The core stays.
- **Tests:** 93 pass, 7 of them new.

**main8, both builds:** `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17`. The Development run had no `Tuning.txt`.

**Shipping run:** title, START, pause and resume in a live room and in a freeze, then QUIT GAME with exit code 0. `-log`/`-abslog=` write nothing in Shipping because it has no engine logging, so I added `-SupercutLog=<file>` and the game writes its own log there. Shipping saves its settings to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Supercut\Saved\Config\Windows\GameUserSettings.ini`.

**Sockets:** none. The Shipping game and its launcher had no listening TCP and no UDP endpoints, so there is nothing to turn off.

**Zip:** `out\SUPERCUT_shipping_test.zip` is 331.6 MB; the folder is 482.4 MB.

**Fixed along the way**
- **Shipping build:** the first Shipping package crashed the compiler on every file. A Shipping precompiled header built through UBA does that with cl.exe 14.44, and the same build without UBA is clean. The package script now passes `-NoUBA`.
- **Menu pictures:** they showed three layout faults, all fixed and re-shot. The FULLSCREEN value touched its arrows, the two controls columns nearly touched, and the room's slate text showed behind PAUSED.

**Not checked:** mouse hover and the cursor showing and hiding, because this PC's rules forbid real input. Scripted keys and clicks are proven, and so is the DISPLAY switch to a 1600x900 window and back.

- Music keeps playing under the pause.
- The title is silent and hides the gun and clapperboard.
- Esc on the title does nothing.
- The overlay darkness: 0.45 on the title, 0.72 elsewhere.

- The benchmark picks the lowest level among its groups.
- The heading "PAUSED" and the controls line "CHOOSE AN UPGRADE".
- The fade distances, 120 cm and 300 cm.

## Scripted game runs depend on frame timing unless the time step is fixed (13 Nov 2026, verified)

- **Trap.** The scripted player (`-SupercutScript`) is timed in game seconds, but each frame's length comes from the
  wall clock. A hitch (another process loading the disk or CPU) makes one frame long, a step lands a few cm off, and a
  run that passed now misses a shot or stops short of a gate. Seen 13 Nov: the same packaged build gave 6 kills, then
  5 while a 1 GB folder copy ran, and a helper's run stopped 5 cm outside a gate.
- **Fix.** `Tools\run_demo.ps1 -FixedFps 240` adds `-UseFixedTimeStep -FPS=240` (both read in
  `Launch/Private/LaunchEngineLoop.cpp`). Every frame then advances game time by exactly 1/240 s. Three packaged runs
  of `run.txt` gave byte-identical `LogSupercut` lines. Use it for every scripted proof.
- **Cost.** Game time no longer matches wall time, so the `FPS rolling` line reads exactly 240. Measure frame rate in a
  run without the switch.

## SUPERCUT feel1 lane: tuning file and practice keys (13 Nov 2026, c4, engine 5.9 preview)

- **F1 to F5 and F9 already do something in a Development game** (13 Nov 2026, verified). Engine `BaseInput.ini`
  `[/Script/Engine.PlayerInput]` has `DebugExecBindings` for them: viewmode wireframe, unlit, lit, lit_detaillighting,
  shadercomplexity, and `shot showui`. `PlayerInput.cpp` runs them in every build but Shipping. To use those keys for
  the game, remove each with a `-DebugExecBindings=` line in the project's `DefaultInput.ini`, copied exactly from
  BaseInput.ini (the `bIgnoreShift=True` on F1 included). `UPlayerInput::GetBind(Key)` returns "" once it is gone.
- **"Next to the exe" is two folders in a packaged build** (13 Nov 2026, verified). The launcher `Supercut.exe` sits
  in the build root, and the real game is `Supercut\Binaries\Win64\Supercut.exe`. `FPaths::RootDir()` (EngineDir with
  `/Engine` cut off) is the build root, the launcher's folder. In an editor build RootDir is the engine folder, so use
  `FPaths::ProjectDir()` there (`#if WITH_EDITOR`).
- **A blanket CRLF `sed` over Source converts files you did not touch** (13 Nov 2026, verified). With
  `core.autocrlf=true` some working files are LF. `sed -i 's/\r\?$/\r/'` on all of them shows no content diff but
  changes them on disk. Convert only the files you edited, and check `file` before and after.

		// A number as a person types it: an optional sign, digits with at most one point, an optional exponent.
		bool IsNumber(const FString& Text, bool& bWhole)
		{
			int32 Index = 0;
			const int32 Len = Text.Len();
			if (Index < Len && (Text[Index] == TEXT('+') || Text[Index] == TEXT('-')))
			{
				++Index;
			}
			int32 Digits = 0;
			bool bPoint = false;
			for (; Index < Len; ++Index)
			{
				const TCHAR C = Text[Index];
				if (FChar::IsDigit(C))
				{
					++Digits;
				}
				else if (C == TEXT('.') && !bPoint)
				{
					bPoint = true;
				}
				else
				{
					break;
				}
			}
			if (Digits == 0)
			{
				return false;
			}
			bool bExponent = false;
			if (Index < Len && (Text[Index] == TEXT('e') || Text[Index] == TEXT('E')))
			{
				bExponent = true;
				++Index;
				if (Index < Len && (Text[Index] == TEXT('+') || Text[Index] == TEXT('-')))
				{
					++Index;
				}
				int32 ExponentDigits = 0;
				for (; Index < Len && FChar::IsDigit(Text[Index]); ++Index)
				{
					++ExponentDigits;
				}
				if (ExponentDigits == 0)
				{
					return false;
				}
			}
			bWhole = !bPoint && !bExponent;
			return Index == Len;
		}
	}

bool SupercutProps::Parse(const FString& File, const TArray<FString>& Lines, TArray<FProp>& Out, FString& Error)
{
	Out.Reset();
	for (int32 Index = 0; Index < Lines.Num(); ++Index)
	{
		const FString Line = Lines[Index].TrimStartAndEnd();
		if (Line.IsEmpty() || Line.StartsWith(TEXT("#")))
		{
			continue;
		}
		FProp Prop;
		FString What = PropsReadLine(Line, Prop);
		if (What.IsEmpty() && Out.ContainsByPredicate([&Prop](const FProp& Each) { return Each.Name == Prop.Name; }))
		{
			What = FString::Printf(TEXT("name=%s is in the catalogue twice"), *Prop.Name);
		}
		if (!What.IsEmpty())
		{
			Error = FString::Printf(TEXT("%s:%d: %s"), *File, Index + 1, *What);
			Out.Reset();
			return false;
		}
		Out.Add(MoveTemp(Prop));
	}
	return true;
}

FString SupercutProps::CataloguePath()
{
	return FPaths::ConvertRelativePathToFull(FPaths::Combine(FPaths::ProjectContentDir(), TEXT("Props"), TEXT("catalogue.txt")));
}

const TArray<SupercutProps::FProp>& SupercutProps::Catalogue()
{
	static TArray<FProp> Props;
	static bool bRead = false;
	if (!bRead)
	{
		const FString File = CataloguePath();
		TArray<FString> Lines;
		if (!FFileHelper::LoadFileToStringArray(Lines, *File))
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Fatal, TEXT("The prop catalogue %s cannot be read. Tools/make_props_real.py writes it."), *File);
		}
		FString Error;
		if (!Parse(File, Lines, Props, Error))
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Fatal, TEXT("Bad prop catalogue line: %s. Tools/make_props_real.py writes this file; run it again."), *Error);
		}
		for (const FProp& Prop : Props)
		{
			Mesh(Prop);
		}
		bRead = true;
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PROPS catalogue: %d props from %s"), Props.Num(), *File);
	}
	return Props;
}

const SupercutProps::FProp* SupercutProps::Find(const FString& Name)
{
	return Catalogue().FindByPredicate([&Name](const FProp& Prop) { return Prop.Name == Name; });
}

FString SupercutProps::Names()
{
	TArray<FString> Names;
	for (const FProp& Prop : Catalogue())
	{
		Names.Add(Prop.Name);
	}
	return FString::Join(Names, TEXT(", "));
}

UStaticMesh* SupercutShapes::Mesh(ESupercutShape Shape)
{
	switch (Shape)
	{
	case ESupercutShape::Cube:     return LoadOrDie<UStaticMesh>(TEXT("/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube.Cube"));

}

int32 USupercutRun::LeaveRoom()
{
	UWorld* World = GetWorld();
	USupercutTime::Get(this).EndScene();

	int32 Removed = 0;
	for (TActorIterator<ASupercutShot> Shot(World); Shot; ++Shot)
	{
		Shot->Destroy();
		++Removed;
	}
	for (TActorIterator<ASupercutChips> Falling(World); Falling; ++Falling)
	{
		Falling->Destroy();   // chips and shells still in the air; the landed ones go with the room
		++Removed;
	}
	if (Room)
	{
		Removed += Room->TearDown();
		Room = nullptr;
	}
	// The engine frees the destroyed actors at the end of this frame, not at some later moment in the next room.
	GEngine->ForceGarbageCollection(true);
	return Removed;
}

void USupercutRun::EnterRoom(int32 Index, bool bNewTake, bool bTitle)
{
	const double Start = FPlatformTime::Seconds();
	UWorld* World = GetWorld();
	APlayerController* Controller = World->GetFirstPlayerController();

	int32 Removed = LeaveRoom();
	if (bNewTake && Hero)
	{
		// A new take is a new player: full health, a full cylinder, nothing carried over.
		if (Controller)
		{
			Controller->UnPossess();
		}
		Hero->Destroy();
		Hero = nullptr;
		++Removed;
	}

	RoomIndex = Index;
	const FSupercutRoomPlan Plan = SupercutRoomFile::LoadOrDie(RoomNames[Index]);
	Room = World->SpawnActor<ASupercutRoom>();
	Room->Build(Plan);

	USupercutTime::Get(this).RefillCharges();
	UsedThisRoom.Reset();
	bFrozeInRoom = false;
	UsedInFreeze.Reset();

	const FRotator Facing(0.f, Room->GetStartYaw(), 0.f);
	if (!Hero)
	{
		FActorSpawnParameters Spawn;
		Spawn.SpawnCollisionHandlingOverride = ESpawnActorCollisionHandlingMethod::AlwaysSpawn;
		Hero = World->SpawnActor<ASupercutCharacter>(Room->GetHeroStart(), Facing, Spawn);
		checkf(Hero, TEXT("USupercutRun: could not spawn the player's character"));
		if (Controller)
		{
			Controller->Possess(Hero);
			Controller->SetControlRotation(Facing);
		}
	}
	else
	{
		Hero->PlaceAt(Room->GetHeroStart(), Room->GetStartYaw());
	}

	RoomSince = World->GetRealTimeSeconds();
	if (bTitle)
	{
		// The backdrop: the room as the first frame of a freeze would show it, the camera still, no sound.
		SetPhase(ESupercutRunPhase::Title);

# Three generated runs to play

Lane gen1, 14 Nov 2026. Twelve rooms each, every room passed the fairness checker.

- `today\` holds the runs without props. Today's game loads these as they are.
- `with_props\` holds the same seeds with props from the 31-prop stand-in catalogue. They need the game's
  catalogue loader, which is not built yet. A room with props and the same room without are two rooms: the
  layout is the same, the cover on fight floors differs.

## Start

Copy `today\Rooms\gen` into `<package>\Supercut\Content\Rooms\` and the three files of `today\Runs` into
`<package>\Supercut\Content\Runs\`. Then, in a Development package, one line per run:

```
Supercut.exe -SupercutRun=gen_s7 -SupercutSeed=7 -SupercutDev -windowed -ResX=1280 -ResY=720

## Size, height and the hall

For the lane that builds the soundstage hall round the rooms. Over 2,000 seeds at 16 depths:

- **Longest room:** @LEN@ cm, outer walls included. The limit in `plan.json` is 9,600 without walls.
- **Widest:** @WID@ cm, outer walls included. Puzzle rooms are 10 to 16 m wide, fights 14 to 18 m.
- **Lowest point:** @ZLOW@ cm. Pits go down; the hall's floor must let them. The start is always at height 0.
- **Highest point of any piece:** @ZTOP@ cm. **Tallest room, lowest to highest point:** @HEI@ cm.
- **Outer walls:** 400 cm above the floor they border (`plan.json`, `wall_height`, the one place to change it).
  Where the floor steps, the wall steps with it. Beside a pit the wall keeps the height of the higher bank.
  The blade tunnel's block is 480 high and stands 80 above the walls beside it. Lamps hang up to 580.
- **Open at the top.** No room has a ceiling, and nothing in a room needs one. The highest a player's head
  gets is about 290 cm above the floor they jumped from (jump 110, capsule 176). A hall with 6 m clear above a
  room's floor is safe at every depth.
- The room's origin is the middle of the start wall on the floor: x runs 0 to the length, y is plus and minus
  the half width, and the walls are 50 thick outside that.

		{
			for (int32 Index = 0; Index < FMath::RoundToInt(Seconds / PropsTestStep); ++Index)
			{
				TickTestWorld(PropsTestStep);
			}
		}

		ASupercutRoom* Room() { return USupercutRun::Get(GetTestWorld()).GetRoom(); }
	};

	/** The room's part that shows this mesh, or null. */
	UStaticMeshComponent* PropsFindMesh(ASupercutRoom* Room, const TCHAR* Mesh)
	{
		TInlineComponentArray<UStaticMeshComponent*> Parts(Room);
		for (UStaticMeshComponent* Part : Parts)
		{
			if (Part->GetStaticMesh() && Part->GetStaticMesh()->GetName() == Mesh)
			{
				return Part;
			}
		}
		return nullptr;
	}
}

void ASupercutPlayerController::RunScript(float DeltaTime, FSupercutInput& Input, ASupercutCharacter* Hero, USupercutRun& Run)
{
	if (bScriptOver)
	{
		return;
	}

	if (Hero->IsDead() && !bDeathExpected)
	{
		FailScript(FString::Printf(TEXT("the player died (%s)"), *Hero->GetDeathCause()));
		return;
	}

	ScriptClock += DeltaTime;
	while (NextStep < Steps.Num() && Steps[NextStep].Time <= ScriptClock)
	{
		const FStep& Step = Steps[NextStep];
		if (Step.Command == TEXT("scene"))
		{
			if (Run.GetRoomEntries() == RoomEntriesSeen)
			{
				// Still in the old room, or on a screen between rooms. Wait here.
				SceneWait += DeltaTime;
				if (SceneWait > SceneWaitLimit)
				{
					FailScript(FString::Printf(TEXT("waited %.0f s at a \"scene\" line and the run did not enter a new room"), SceneWaitLimit));
					return;
				}
				break;
			}
			const int32 WantScene = Step.Args.IsValidIndex(0) ? FCString::Atoi(*Step.Args[0]) : 0;
			const int32 WantTake = Step.Args.IsValidIndex(1) ? FCString::Atoi(*Step.Args[1]) : Run.GetTake();
			if (WantScene != Run.GetScene() || WantTake != Run.GetTake())
			{
				FailScript(FString::Printf(TEXT("the script expected scene %d take %d and the run is in scene %d take %d"), WantScene, WantTake, Run.GetScene(), Run.GetTake()));
				return;
			}
			RoomEntriesSeen = Run.GetRoomEntries();
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("SCRIPT scene %d take %d entered after %.2f s, clock set to 0"), Run.GetScene(), Run.GetTake(), ScriptClock);
			ScriptClock = 0.f;
			SceneWait = 0.f;
			HeldForward = 0.f;
			HeldRight = 0.f;
			bHeldFire = false;
			bDeathExpected = false;
			++NextStep;
			continue;
		}

		RunStep(Step, Input, Hero);
		++NextStep;
		if (bScriptOver)
		{
			return;
		}
	}
	Input.Forward = HeldForward;
	Input.Right = HeldRight;
	Input.bFire = Input.bFire || bHeldFire;
}

{
	SetControlRotation((Point - Hero->GetEyeLocation()).Rotation());
}

import sys, glob, os
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
src, out, cols = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 4
pat = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else "*.png"
files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(src, pat)))
W = 480; H = 270
rows = (len(files) + cols - 1) // cols
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (cols * W, rows * (H + 18)), (40, 40, 40))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
for i, f in enumerate(files):
    im = Image.open(f).convert("RGB").resize((W, H))
    x, y = (i % cols) * W, (i // cols) * (H + 18)
    sheet.paste(im, (x, y + 18)); d.text((x + 4, y + 3), os.path.basename(f), fill=(255, 255, 255))
sheet.save(out, quality=85)
print(len(files), sheet.size)
EOF

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

/**
 * Tuning.txt: the numbers of FSupercutTuning, changed without a rebuild.
 *
 * The file holds one "Name = value" per line; # starts a comment, blank lines are skipped. Names are the struct's
 * field names. It is read when the game starts (ASupercutGameMode::InitGame) and again on the practice key F5.
 * Each read starts from the struct's defaults, so a line taken out of the file goes back to its default.
 * With no file every number is its default.
 *
 * A bad line (no "=", an unknown name, a value that is not a number, a number with a fraction for a whole-number
 * field, a value outside the field's range, a name given twice) is not applied. It is listed in the log and drawn
 * in red by the HUD; the good lines still apply. The game goes on: a person edits this file by hand.
 *
 * The file sits next to Supercut.exe: in a packaged build the folder that holds Supercut.exe, Engine and
 * Supercut (FPaths::RootDir); in an editor build the project folder.
 * "Supercut.exe -SupercutWriteTuning" writes Tuning.example.txt there, every field with its default and the
 * header's comment, and quits.

		double Lowest;                           // the lowest value Tuning.txt may set; a value outside is a bad line
		double Highest;                          // the highest
	};
	/** The list, sections included. */
	const TArray<FEntry>& Entries();

The hall kit comes from lane hall1 through Tools/make_props_real.py.\"),\n\t\t\t\tName, *SupercutProps::CataloguePath());\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn { Prop, SupercutProps::Mesh(*Prop) };\n\t}\n\n\t/** The four hall walls. Yaw turns a kit piece's +X to Inward. */\n\tstruct FHallSide\n\t{\n\t\tFVector Start;\n\t\tFVector Along;\n\t\tFVector Inward;\n\t\tfloat Length;\n\t\tfloat Yaw;\n\n\t\tFVector At(float U, float D, float Z) const { return FVector(Start.X, Start.Y, Z) + Along * U + Inward * D; }\n\t};\n\n\t/** Yaw that turns a corner piece's two open ends (its -X and +Y edges) to face A and B, whichever way round fits. */\n\tfloat HallCornerYaw(const FVector& A, const FVector& B)\n\t{\n\t\tfor (int32 Turn = 0; Turn < 4; ++Turn)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tconst FRotator R(0.f, Turn * 90.f, 0.f);\n\t\t\tconst FVector MinusX = R.RotateVector(-FVector::XAxisVector);\n\t\t\tconst FVector PlusY = R.RotateVector(FVector::YAxisVector);\n\t\t\tif ((MinusX.Equals(A, 0.01) && PlusY.Equals(B, 0.01)) || (MinusX.Equals(B, 0.01) && PlusY.Equals(A, 0.01)))\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\treturn Turn * 90.f;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tcheckf(false, TEXT(\"Hall: no corner turn joins %s and %s\"), *A.ToCompactString(), *B.ToCompactString());\n\t\treturn 0.f;\n\t}\n\n\t/** The layout as it is made: every piece's transform by catalogue name, kept out of the room. */\n\tstruct FHallLayout\n\t{\n\t\tFBox Keep;                 // the room's box plus the margin: nothing but floor tiles in it\n\t\tTArray<FBox> RoomParts;    // the room's solid parts: a floor tile lies under each it overlaps\n\t\tTArray<FBox> Props;        // the room's parts that do not collide (the desk lamp, desk things): no piece crosses one\n\t\tfloat FloorZ = 0.f;\n\t\tTMap<FString, FHallPiece> Pieces;\n\t\tTMap<FString, TArray<FTransform>> Placed;\n\t\tTArray<FTransform> Lenses;   // lamp lenses that glow\n\t\tint32 Dropped = 0;\n\n\t\tconst FHallPiece& Piece(const TCHAR* Name)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tif (const FHallPiece* Found = Pieces.Find(Name))\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\treturn *Found;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\treturn Pieces.Add(Name, HallPiece(Name));\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t/** Adds a piece unless it would stand in the room's box plus the margin or cross a room part that does not collide. */\n\t\tbool Add(const TCHAR* Name, const FVector& At, float Yaw)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tconst FTransform Where(FRotator(0.f, Yaw, 0.f), At);\n\t\t\tconst FBox Box = Piece(Name).Mesh->GetBoundingBox().TransformBy(Where);\n\t\t\tbool bClear = !Box.Intersect(Keep);\n\t\t\tfor (const FBox& Prop : Props)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tbClear = bClear && !Box.Intersect(Prop);\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif (!bClear)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\t++Dropped;\n\t\t\t\treturn false;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tPlaced.FindOrAdd(Name).Add(Where);\n\t\t\treturn true;\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t/** A floor tile goes wherever no solid part of the room it lies under reaches below the hall floor. */\n\t\tvoid AddFloor(const TCHAR* Name, const FVector& At, float Yaw)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tconst FBox Cell(At - FVector(HallCell * 0.5f - 1.f, HallCell * 0.5f - 1.f, 0.f), At + FVector(HallCell * 0.5f - 1.f, HallCell * 0.5f - 1.f, 0.f));\n\t\t\tfor (const FBox& Part : RoomParts)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tconst bool bOver = Part.Min.X < Cell.Max.X && Part.Max.X > Cell.Min.X && Part.Min.Y < Cell.Max.Y && Part.Max.Y > Cell.Min.Y;\n\t\t\t\tif (bOver && Part.Min.Z < FloorZ - 1.f)\n\t\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\t\treturn;   // a pit or a lower floor: the tile would cover it\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tPlaced.FindOrAdd(Name).Add(FTransform(FRotator(0.f, Yaw, 0.f), At));\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t/** A hanging lamp; a lit one also gets a glowing lens. */\n\t\tvoid AddLamp(const TCHAR* Name, const FVector& At, float Yaw, bool bLit)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tif (!Add(Name, At, Yaw) || !bLit)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\treturn;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tconst SupercutProps::FProp& Prop = *Piece(Name).Prop;\n\t\t\tcheckf(Prop.bHasLens, TEXT(\"Hall lamp %s has no lens= in the catalogue\"), *Prop.Name);\n\t\t\tconst FRotator Turn(0.f, Yaw, 0.f);\n\t\t\t// The beam: along the lamp's +X, tilted down by its tilt; a lamp with tilt 0 hangs and lights straight down.\n\t\t\tconst FVector Beam = Prop.Tilt > 0.f ? Turn.RotateVector(FRotator(-Prop.Tilt, 0.f, 0.f).Vector()) : -FVector::ZAxisVector;\n\t\t\tconst float Across = FMath::Min(Prop.Size.X, Prop.Size.Y) * 0.7f;\n\t\t\tLenses.Add(FTransform(FRotationMatrix::MakeFromZ(Beam).Rotator(), At + Turn.RotateVector(Prop.Lens) + Beam * 1.5f, FVector(Across, Across, 3.f) / 100.f));\n\t\t}\n\t};\n}\n\nASupercutHall::ASupercutHall()\n{\n\tPrimaryActorTick.bCanEverTick = false;\n\tRootComponent = CreateDefaultSubobject<USceneComponent>(TEXT(\"Root\"));\n\tRootComponent->SetMobility(EComponentMobility::Static);\n}\n\nASupercutHall* ASupercutHall::BuildFor(ASupercutRoom& Room)\n{\n\tconst FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();\n\tif (Tuning.HallOn == 0)\n\t{\n\t\treturn nullptr;\n\t}\n\n\t// ---- What the room is: its solid box, the floor under its start, its loose parts, the dark studio round it.\n\tFHallLayout L;\n\tFBox Studio(ForceInit);\n\tTInlineComponentArray<UPrimitiveComponent*> Parts(&Room);\n\tfor (const UPrimitiveComponent* Part : Parts)\n\t{\n\t\tconst FBox Box = Part->Bounds.GetBox();\n\t\tif (Part->bRenderCustomDepth && Part->CustomDepthStencilValue == static_cast<int32>(SupercutShapes::ESketch::Studio))\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tStudio += Box;\n\t\t}\n\t\telse if (Part->IsCollisionEnabled())\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tL.RoomParts.Add(Box);\n\t\t}\n\t\telse if (Cast<UStaticMeshComponent>(Part))\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tL.Props.Add(Box.ExpandBy(50.f));\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tconst FBox RoomBox = Room.GetComponentsBoundingBox();\n\tcheckf(RoomBox.IsValid && Studio.IsValid, TEXT(\"Hall: room %s has no solid parts or no dark studio round it\"), *Room.GetRoomName());\n\n\tconst FVector StartFloor = Room.GetHeroStart() - FVector(0.f, 0.f, 100.f);\n\tconst FBox* Under = nullptr;\n\tfor (const FBox& Part : L.RoomParts)\n\t{\n\t\tconst bool bUnder = StartFloor.X > Part.Min.X && StartFloor.X < Part.Max.X && StartFloor.Y > Part.Min.Y && StartFloor.Y < Part.Max.Y && Part.Max.Z <= StartFloor.Z + 1.f;\n\t\tif (bUnder && (!Under || Part.Max.Z > Under->Max.Z))\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tUnder = &Part;\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tcheckf(Under, TEXT(\"Hall: room %s has no floor under its start at %s\"), *Room.GetRoomName(), *StartFloor.ToCompactString());\n\tL.FloorZ = Under->Min.Z;\n\tL.Keep = RoomBox.ExpandBy(Tuning.HallMargin);\n\n\t// ---- The hall's own random stream, from the room's name.\n\tFRandomStream Stream(static_cast<int32>(FCrc::StrCrc32(*Room.GetRoomName())));\n\n\t// The grid box round the kept-out box: the truss rig runs on its edges.\n\tauto Down = [](double V) { return FMath::FloorToDouble(V / HallCell) * HallCell; };\n\tauto Up = [](double V) { return FMath::CeilToDouble(V / HallCell) * HallCell; };\n\tconst FVector2D GridMin(Down(L.Keep.Min.X - 50.0), Down(L.Keep.Min.Y - 50.0));\n\tconst FVector2D GridMax(Up(L.Keep.Max.X + 50.0), Up(L.Keep.Max.Y + 50.0));\n\n\t// Walls: one near wall 3 cells out from the rig, the others 4 to 6; far enough to hold the desk lamp and every\n\t// loose part of the room with a cell to spare; inside the dark studio, at least 2 cells out.\n\tconst int32 Near = Stream.RandRange(0, 3);\n\tdouble Gap[4];\n\tfor (int32 Side = 0; Side < 4; ++Side)\n\t{\n\t\tGap[Side] = HallCell * (Side == Near ? 3 : Stream.RandRange(4, 6));\n\t}\n\tdouble X0 = GridMin.X - Gap[0], Y0 = GridMin.Y - Gap[1], X1 = GridMax.X + Gap[2], Y1 = GridMax.Y + Gap[3];\n\tdouble TallTop = RoomBox.Max.Z;\n\tfor (const FBox& Prop : L.Props)\n\t{\n\t\tX0 = FMath::Min(X0, Down(Prop.Min.X - HallCell));\n\t\tY0 = FMath::Min(Y0, Down(Prop.Min.Y - HallCell));\n\t\tX1 = FMath::Max(X1, Up(Prop.Max.X + HallCell));\n\t\tY1 = FMath::Max(Y1, Up(Prop.Max.Y + HallCell));\n\t\tTallTop = FMath::Max(TallTop, Prop.Max.Z);\n\t}\n\tconst double WallBack = 60.0;   // the thickest wall piece stands 46 cm behind its face\n\tX0 = FMath::Max(X0, Up(Studio.Min.X + WallBack));\n\tY0 = FMath::Max(Y0, Up(Studio.Min.Y + WallBack));\n\tX1 = FMath::Min(X1, Down(Studio.Max.X - WallBack));\n\tY1 = FMath::Min(Y1, Down(Studio.Max.Y - WallBack));\n\tcheckf(GridMin.X - X0 >= 2 * HallCell && GridMin.Y - Y0 >= 2 * HallCell && X1 - GridMax.X >= 2 * HallCell && Y1 - GridMax.Y >= 2 * HallCell,\n\t\tTEXT(\"Hall: room %s leaves less than two cells between the set and the dark studio (HallMargin %.0f)\"), *Room.GetRoomName(), Tuning.HallMargin);\n\n\t// Heights: the rig hangs its lamps clear above the kept-out box; the roof clears the rig, the tallest part of the\n\t// room (the desk lamp) and HallHeight. One wall row in two halls is extra.\n\tconst float FloorZ = L.FloorZ;\n\tconst int32 RigRows = FMath::Max(3, FMath::CeilToInt((L.Keep.Max.Z + 180.f - FloorZ) / HallCell));\n\tconst float RigZ = FloorZ + RigRows * HallCell;\n\tconst double Clear = FMath::Max3(double(Tuning.HallHeight), TallTop + HallCell - FloorZ, RigZ + 2 * HallCell - FloorZ);\n\tconst int32 Rows = FMath::CeilToInt(Clear / HallCell) + Stream.RandRange(0, 1);\n\tconst float RoofZ = FloorZ + Rows * HallCell;\n\tcheckf(RoofZ + 250.f < Studio.Max.Z, TEXT(\"Hall: room %s: the roof at %.0f would stand above the dark studio's top at %.0f\"), *Room.GetRoomName(), RoofZ, Studio.Max.Z);\n\n\tconst FHallSide Sides[4] =\n\t{\n\t\t{ FVector(X0, Y0, 0), FVector::YAxisVector, FVector::XAxisVector, float(Y1 - Y0), 0.f },\n\t\t{ FVector(X0, Y0, 0), FVector::XAxisVector, FVector::YAxisVector, float(X1 - X0), 90.f },\n\t\t{ FVector(X1, Y0, 0), FVector::YAxisVector, -FVector::XAxisVector, float(Y1 - Y0), 180.f },\n\t\t{ FVector(X0, Y1, 0), FVector::XAxisVector, -FVector::YAxisVector, float(X1 - X0), 270.f },\n\t};\n\n\t// ---- Floor: plain concrete, with a white tape line round the rig.\n\tfor (double X = X0 + HallCell * 0.5; X < X1; X += HallCell)\n\t{\n\t\tfor (double Y = Y0 + HallCell * 0.5; Y < Y1; Y += HallCell)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tconst bool bLineX = FMath::IsNearlyEqual(X, GridMin.X - HallCell * 0.5) || FMath::IsNearlyEqual(X, GridMax.X + HallCell * 0.5);\n\t\t\tconst bool bLineY = FMath::IsNearlyEqual(Y, GridMin.Y - HallCell * 0.5) || FMath::IsNearlyEqual(Y, GridMax.Y + HallCell * 0.5);\n\t\t\tconst bool bInX = X > GridMin.X - HallCell && X < GridMax.X + HallCell;\n\t\t\tconst bool bInY = Y > GridMin.Y - HallCell && Y < GridMax.Y + HallCell;\n\t\t\tconst FVector At(X, Y, FloorZ);\n\t\t\tif (bLineX && bLineY)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tconst FVector ToX(X < GridMin.X ? 1.0 : -1.0, 0, 0), ToY(0, Y < GridMin.Y ? 1.0 : -1.0, 0);\n\t\t\t\tL.AddFloor(TEXT(\"hall_floor_line_corner\"), At, HallCornerYaw(ToX, ToY));\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\telse if (bLineX && bInY)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tL.AddFloor(TEXT(\"hall_floor_line\"), At, 90.f);\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\telse if (bLineY && bInX)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tL.AddFloor(TEXT(\"hall_floor_line\"), At, 0.f);\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\telse\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tL.AddFloor(TEXT(\"hall_floor\"), At, 0.f);\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// ---- Walls: plain at the foot and the top, a band of padding, steel columns every second joint, corner piers,\n\t// one stage door (4 cells wide, 2 high) on a wall of the stream's choosing.\n\tconst int32 DoorSide = Stream.RandRange(0, 3);\n\tconst int32 DoorCells = FMath::FloorToInt(Sides[DoorSide].Length / HallCell);\n\tcheckf(DoorCells >= 8, TEXT(\"Hall: room %s: a wall of %d cells is too short for the stage door\"), *Room.GetRoomName(), DoorCells);\n\tconst float DoorU = HallCell * Stream.RandRange(4, DoorCells - 4);   // the door's middle, on a joint\n\tconst int32 PadTop = FMath::Min(Rows - 1, Stream.RandRange(2, 4));\n\tfor (int32 Side = 0; Side < 4; ++Side)\n\t{\n\t\tconst FHallSide& S = Sides[Side];\n\t\tconst int32 Cells = FMath::RoundToInt(S.Length / HallCell);\n\t\tfor (int32 Row = 0; Row < Rows; ++Row)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tconst float Z = FloorZ + Row * HallCell;\n\t\t\tfor (int32 Cell = 0; Cell < Cells; ++Cell)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tconst float U = (Cell + 0.5f) * HallCell;\n\t\t\t\tif (Side == DoorSide && Row < 2 && FMath::Abs(U - DoorU) < 2 * HallCell)\n\t\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tL.Add(Row >= 1 && Row <= PadTop ? TEXT(\"hall_wall_padded\") : TEXT(\"hall_wall_plain\"), S.At(U, 0.f, Z), S.Yaw);\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tfor (int32 Joint = 2; Joint < Cells; Joint += 2)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tconst float U = Joint * HallCell;\n\t\t\t\tif (!(Side == DoorSide && Row < 2 && FMath::Abs(U - DoorU) < 2 * HallCell))\n\t\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_wall_column\"), S.At(U, 0.f, Z), S.Yaw);\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_wall_corner\"), S.At(0.f, 0.f, Z), S.Yaw);\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t{\n\t\tconst FHallSide& S = Sides[DoorSide];\n\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_wall_door\"), S.At(DoorU, 0.f, FloorZ), S.Yaw);\n\t\tconst FVector DoorClosed(11.f, -300.f, 0.f);   // SM_Hall_Wall_Door.json, door_closed\n\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_stage_door\"), S.At(DoorU, 0.f, FloorZ) + FRotator(0.f, S.Yaw, 0.f).RotateVector(DoorClosed), S.Yaw);\n\t}\n\n\t// ---- Catwalk round the walls at 8 m, on trestles under every second span; no trestle in front of the door.\n\tconst float WalkZ = FloorZ + 2 * HallCell;\n\tfor (int32 Side = 0; Side < 4; ++Side)\n\t{\n\t\tconst FHallSide& S = Sides[Side];\n\t\tconst int32 Cells = FMath::RoundToInt(S.Length / HallCell);\n\t\tfor (int32 Cell = 1; Cell < Cells - 1; ++Cell)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tconst float U = (Cell + 0.5f) * HallCell;\n\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_straight\"), S.At(U, HallCell * 0.5f, WalkZ), S.Yaw + 90.f);\n\t\t\tconst bool bByDoor = Side == DoorSide && FMath::Abs(U - DoorU) < 2 * HallCell + 100.f;\n\t\t\tif (Cell % 2 == 1 && !bByDoor)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_post\"), S.At(U, HallCell * 0.5f, FloorZ), S.Yaw + 90.f);\n\t\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_post\"), S.At(U, HallCell * 0.5f, FloorZ + HallCell), S.Yaw + 90.f);\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\t// The corner where this wall starts: its run goes along Along, the other wall's run along Inward.\n\t\tconst FVector Corner = S.At(HallCell * 0.5f, HallCell * 0.5f, WalkZ);\n\t\tif (Side == 0 || Side == 1)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\t// Sides 0 and 1 share the corner at X0, Y0; side 0 places it.\n\t\t\tif (Side == 0)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_corner\"), Corner, HallCornerYaw(S.Along, S.Inward));\n\t\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_post\"), FVector(Corner.X, Corner.Y, FloorZ), 45.f);\n\t\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_post\"), FVector(Corner.X, Corner.Y, FloorZ + HallCell), 45.f);\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\telse\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_corner\"), Corner, HallCornerYaw(S.Along, S.Inward));\n\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_post\"), FVector(Corner.X, Corner.Y, FloorZ), 45.f);\n\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_post\"), FVector(Corner.X, Corner.Y, FloorZ + HallCell), 45.f);\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t{\n\t\t// The fourth corner, X1 Y1: the end of side 2's run.\n\t\tconst FVector Corner(X1 - HallCell * 0.5, Y1 - HallCell * 0.5, WalkZ);\n\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_corner\"), Corner, HallCornerYaw(-FVector::XAxisVector, -FVector::YAxisVector));\n\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_post\"), FVector(Corner.X, Corner.Y, FloorZ), 45.f);\n\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_catwalk_post\"), FVector(Corner.X, Corner.Y, FloorZ + HallCell), 45.f);\n\t}\n\n\t// ---- Scaffold towers and stacked gear, in the second cell out from the walls, never in front of the door.\n\tTArray<TPair<int32, float>> Taken;   // side, U of each used spot\n\tauto SpotFree = [&](int32 Side, float U)\n\t{\n\t\tconst float Length = Sides[Side].Length;\n\t\tif (U < 2 * HallCell || U > Length - 2 * HallCell || (Side == DoorSide && FMath::Abs(U - DoorU) < 3 * HallCell))\n\t\t{\n\t\t\treturn false;\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor (const TPair<int32, float>& Used : Taken)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tif (Used.Key == Side && FMath::Abs(Used.Value - U) < 3 * HallCell)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\treturn false;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn true;\n\t};\n\tauto PickSpot = [&](int32& OutSide, float& OutU)\n\t{\n\t\tfor (int32 Try = 0; Try < 40; ++Try)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tOutSide = Stream.RandRange(0, 3);\n\t\t\tOutU = HallCell * (Stream.RandRange(2, FMath::RoundToInt(Sides[OutSide].Length / HallCell) - 2) + 0.5f);\n\t\t\tif (SpotFree(OutSide, OutU))\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tTaken.Add({ OutSide, OutU });\n\t\t\t\treturn true;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false;\n\t};\n\tconst int32 Towers = Stream.RandRange(2, 4);\n\tfor (int32 Tower = 0; Tower < Towers; ++Tower)\n\t{\n\t\tint32 Side;\n\t\tfloat U;\n\t\tif (!PickSpot(Side, U))\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst FHallSide& S = Sides[Side];\n\t\tconst int32 Storeys = Stream.RandRange(4, 7);\n\t\tfor (int32 Storey = 0; Storey < Storeys; ++Storey)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tconst FVector At = S.At(U, HallCell * 1.5f, FloorZ + Storey * HallCell * 0.5f);\n\t\t\tL.Add(Storey == 0 ? TEXT(\"hall_scaffold_base\") : Storey % 2 ? TEXT(\"hall_scaffold_braced\") : TEXT(\"hall_scaffold_section\"), At, S.Yaw);\n\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_scaffold_ladder\"), At, S.Yaw);\n\t\t\tif (Storey == Storeys / 2)\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_scaffold_deck\"), At, S.Yaw);\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_scaffold_top\"), S.At(U, HallCell * 1.5f, FloorZ + Storeys * HallCell * 0.5f), S.Yaw);\n\t}\n\tconst int32 Stacks = Stream.RandRange(2, 4);\n\tfor (int32 Stack = 0; Stack < Stacks; ++Stack)\n\t{\n\t\tint32 Side;\n\t\tfloat U;\n\t\tif (!PickSpot(Side, U))\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t}\n\t\tconst FHallSide& S = Sides[Side];\n\t\t// Along the wall: two stacked road cases, a single case, then pallets or drums. D is the distance from the wall.\n\t\tstruct FGear { const TCHAR* Name; float U; float D; float Yaw; };\n\t\tconst FGear Gear[] =\n\t\t{\n\t\t\t{ TEXT(\"road_case_stack\"),  -130.f, 500.f, 90.f },\n\t\t\t{ TEXT(\"road_case_stack\"),   -20.f, 500.f, 90.f },\n\t\t\t{ TEXT(\"road_case_single\"),   95.f, 505.f, 90.f },\n\t\t\t{ Stream.FRand() < 0.5f ? TEXT(\"pallet_stack\") : TEXT(\"plastic_crates\"), 30.f, 650.f, 0.f },\n\t\t\t{ TEXT(\"steel_drum\"),        170.f, 640.f, 0.f },\n\t\t};\n\t\tfor (const FGear& G : Gear)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tL.Add(G.Name, S.At(U + G.U, G.D, FloorZ), S.Yaw + G.Yaw + Stream.FRandRange(-6.f, 6.f));\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// ---- The rig: box truss on the edges of the grid box at RigZ, cross runs over the set every 3 cells, legs at the\n\t// corners and on every second cross run, lamps on the inner chord pointing at the set, space lights over the set.\n\tconst float LitShare = Stream.FRandRange(0.35f, 0.65f);\n\tauto Run = [&](const FVector& From, int32 Cells, bool bAlongX)\n\t{\n\t\tfor (int32 Cell = 0; Cell < Cells; ++Cell)\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tL.Add(TEXT(\"hall_truss_400\"), From + (bAlongX ? def ssh(host, cmd, data=None):

    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit(f"FARM ssh {host} failed ({r.returncode}): {cmd}\n{r.stderr.decode(errors='replace')}")
    return r.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def main():
    host, root, name, proj = sys.argv[1:5]
    proj = os.path.abspath(proj)
    if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(proj, "Supercut.uproject")):
        sys.exit(f"FARM no Supercut.uproject in {proj}")
    dest = f"{root}\\Farm\\{name}"
    t0 = time.time()
    remote = {}

        rel, size, mtime = line.rsplit("|", 2)
        remote[rel] = (int(size), int(mtime))
    local = {}
    for top in os.listdir(proj):
        if top in SKIP:
            continue
        p = os.path.join(proj, top)
        if os.path.isfile(p):
            st = os.stat(p)
            local[top] = (st.st_size, int(st.st_mtime))
            continue
        for d, dirs, files in os.walk(p):
            for f in files:
                full = os.path.join(d, f)
                st = os.stat(full)
                local[os.path.relpath(full, proj).replace("\\", "/")] = (st.st_size, int(st.st_mtime))
    send = sorted(r for r, v in local.items() if remote.get(r) != v)

    if send:

import sys, glob, os
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
src, out, cols = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 4
pat = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else "*.png"
files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(src, pat)))
W = 480; H = 270
rows = (len(files) + cols - 1) // cols
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (cols * W, rows * (H + 18)), (40, 40, 40))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
for i, f in enumerate(files):
    im = Image.open(f).convert("RGB").resize((W, H))
    x, y = (i % cols) * W, (i // cols) * (H + 18)
    sheet.paste(im, (x, y + 18)); d.text((x + 4, y + 3), os.path.basename(f), fill=(255, 255, 255))
sheet.save(out, quality=85)
print(len(files), sheet.size)

			SupercutShapes::Glow(Hall, LensColor, HallLensGlow * Tuning.HallLampStrength), L.Lenses);
	}

	// ---- Two work lights high on opposite walls, so the hall's far side reads. They reach no nearer than a metre
	// from the kept-out box, so the set's light is the room's alone.
	int32 Lights = 0;
	if (Tuning.HallLampStrength > 0.f)
	{
		for (const int32 Side : { Near, (Near + 2) % 4 })
		{
			const FHallSide& S = Sides[Side];
			const FVector At = S.At(S.Length * 0.5f, HallCell * 2.f, FloorZ + 3.5f * HallCell);
			const float Reach = FMath::Min(2800.f, FMath::Sqrt(L.Keep.ComputeSquaredDistanceToPoint(At)) - 100.f);
			if (Reach < HallCell)
			{
				continue;
			}
			UPointLightComponent* Light = NewObject<UPointLightComponent>(Hall);
			Light->SetMobility(EComponentMobility::Movable);
			Light->SetupAttachment(Hall->GetRootComponent());
			Light->SetWorldLocation(At);
			Light->IntensityUnits = ELightUnits::Candelas;
			Light->Intensity = 60.f * Tuning.HallLampStrength;
			Light->bUseTemperature = true;
			Light->Temperature = 4800.f;
			Light->AttenuationRadius = Reach;
			Light->SourceRadius = 60.f;
			Light->CastShadows = false;
			Light->RegisterComponent();
			Hall->AddInstanceComponent(Light);
			++Lights;
		}
	}

	// ---- Haze: height fog from the hall floor, thin enough that the set stays clear and the far walls sit back.
	if (Tuning.HallHaze > 0.f)
	{
		UExponentialHeightFogComponent* Haze = NewObject<UExponentialHeightFogComponent>(Hall);
		Haze->SetupAttachment(Hall->GetRootComponent());
		Haze->SetWorldLocation(FVector((X0 + X1) * 0.5, (Y0 + Y1) * 0.5, FloorZ));
		Haze->FogDensity = Tuning.HallHaze;
		Haze->FogHeightFalloff = 0.05f;
		Haze->FogInscatteringLuminance = FLinearColor(0.045f, 0.043f, 0.040f);
		Haze->StartDistance = 1200.f;
		Haze->RegisterComponent();
		Hall->AddInstanceComponent(Haze);
	}
